lines.text: Not all at once, but in small things you only notice when you visit.
Your dad takes the stairs a little slower now.
Your mom tells you the same story twice, and you pretend it's the first time.
Their hands look older than you remember.
They still save the best piece of dinner for you.
They still wait for your call on Sundays, even if they'd never say it.
And somewhere along the way, the roles quietly switched.
Now they ask you how their phone works.
Now you're the one who worries when they drive at night.
Nobody warns you about this part of growing up.
You spend years trying to leave home, then years wishing for one more ordinary afternoon there.
They won't be here forever. But they're here today.
So call them. Ask about the old stories. Let them tell you twice.
Because one day, those stories will be yours to tell.

post.caption: The roles switch so quietly you almost miss it. When did you last call them just to talk? 🤍
